thread:
maria: FYI: noticed a ~1.6x p50 token latency bump on staging after merging PR #6789. Looks concentrated in the KV-batcher -> kernel selection hotpath. Perfetto attached. Can someone triage?

noah: Ugh. Can you drop the before/after traces and a short summary (p50/p95 tokens)?

maria: Before (main@a1b2c3): p50=18ms/token, p95=42ms. After (post-PR): p50=29ms/token, p95=78ms. Traces: before: https://perfetto.local/trace/212987-before  after: https://perfetto.local/trace/212987-after

maria: Quick nsys summary (after):
```
nsys-summary:
  total-kernel-time: 720ms
  multihead_attention_fwd: 410ms (single largest)
  attention_kv_cache_copy: 82ms
  kernel-launch-overhead: 38ms
```
There is a long contiguous span where the runtime picks the larger MHA kernel variant repeatedly.

elaine: Any change to the kernel selection heuristic in that PR? I remember #6789 touched the batcher scoring to prefer "fast-path" kernels when batch shapes are skewed.

maria: Yes, the PR altered the selector to add a fragmentation penalty to small packed batches, and also introduced a tie-breaker that prefers the high-throughput kernel if estimated throughput delta > 25%. That tie-breaker looks like it might be mis-estimating for KV-backed prefixes.

ajay: Can you paste the selector snippet? Even a one-liner. Also, did you capture KV cache hit/miss rates in the trace?

maria: Selector diff (simplified):
```
if (throughput_delta > 0.25) choose(high_throughput_kernel);
if (fragmentation > 0.15) penalize(small_kernel);
```
KV stats (from runtime logs during the run):
```
kv.prefix_hits: 0.62
kv.prefix_misses: 0.38
kv.evictions: 112
kv.cache_size: 384MB
```
Note the prefix_hits down from 0.88 in the before run.

noah: That hit-rate drop is suspicious — could the selector be changing request shaping so the cache keys differ? Or are we evicting more aggressively?

maria: I grepped the logs: the batcher started aggregating more variable-length requests into a single packed batch, which seems to change prefix alignment. There are a lot more partial-key lookups:  E.g. log lines: `kv_lookup: partial_key=true missing_suffixes=3`.

ajay: Can you try an nsys with NVTX around the batcher+kv lookup and the kernel selector? Run: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=run_after.nsys ./reproducer --trace-markers` and attach the resulting .qdrep. Also run a before/after with `--kv-debug` to dump key hashes.

perf-bot: nsys job queued: job-id=perf-4578, started at 2129876600, qdrep=/nfs/perf/2129876600.qdrep

maria: I also ran a quick git bisect on the staging branch. The first bad commit shown: 9f1a2c3 (adaptive-batcher: prefer-high-throughput-kernel). Bisect output: `good: main@a1b2c3 ; bad: 9f1a2c3`

elaine: Good find. That commit message matches the added tie-breaker. Can you try reverting that tie-breaker locally and re-run the reproducer? If it's the culprit we should see p50 drop back near baseline.

maria: Reverted the tie-breaker locally and reran. Results: p50=19ms/token, p95=44ms. nsys summary shows MHA kernel time back to ~220ms. So looks like the heuristic misfires for KV-prefixed workloads.

ajay: That strongly suggests the throughput estimator isn't accounting for KV-cache-induced shape fragmentation or additional copy cost. Two quick fixes: 1) reduce the throughput threshold (0.25 -> 0.4) so we only pick HT kernel when it's very clear, or 2) include an estimated kv-copy penalty when computing throughput_delta.

noah: I can run a microbenchmark to measure the per-request KV copy overhead for partial-key cases. If we can quantify it we can add it into selector's cost model.

maria: Patch suggestion (local):
```
- if (throughput_delta > 0.25) choose(high_throughput_kernel);
+ if (throughput_delta > 0.35 && kv_partial_penalty < throughput_delta) choose(high_throughput_kernel);
```
I can open a hotfix PR to revert the tie-breaker until we have a measured penalty model.

elaine: Please do the hotfix PR and run the staging smoke once merged. Also add an automated perf-test that runs the KV-prefixed reproducer in CI so this doesn't regress silently.

ajay: I'll run the NVTX instrumented traces and share the qdrep once perf-bot finishes. Also will run the microbench for kv-copy overhead.

perf-bot: nsys job completed: job-id=perf-4578, qdrep=/nfs/perf/2129876600.qdrep, perfetto-link=https://perfetto.local/qdrep/2129876600

noah: Thanks. Next steps: 1) maria open hotfix PR to revert tie-breaker, 2) ajay collect kv-copy microbench, 3) add CI workload for KV-prefixed path. If everyone agrees I'll mark this P1 until hotfix lands.

maria: Agree. I'll draft the PR now and tag you all. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
